messages:
Marisol Cardenas: heads up — canary-01 reported ~56 OOMs during pool-shrink repro at 03:42 UTC. Heap traces point at inconsistent pmap entries after pool shrink. Repro steps below, can someone take heapshots + perf? Thanks.

Jon Patel: pinging @Li Wei and @Tanya — I can grab heapshots, do you want them from the canary or the repro harness?

Li Wei: canary first; reproducer might hammer a race. Also, if you can include /proc/kcore dmesg snippet that helps. Example repro command I used:
```
./tools/repro --scenario=shrink-heavy --clients=48 --alloc-pattern=rand-32k
sleep 10; ./bin/heapshot --out=/tmp/shot1.json
```

sam-runtime-bot: deploy event: canary-01 image v2026.3.7 rolled at 2066543230. No config changes.

Jon Patel: grabbing heapshots now. also adding perf script (/scripts/pagemap-scan.sh) — it dumps `pagemap` for PID and checks for non-canonical mappings. dropping here in case it's useful:
```
#!/bin/bash
pid=$1
offset=0
while read -r start end flags; do
  sudo awk "{print \\$1}" /proc/$pid/pagemap | sed -n "${offset},${offset}+100p"
  offset=$((offset+100))
done < /proc/$pid/maps
```

Tanya Ortiz: quick idea — we recently changed `pool_shrink()` to coalesce spans lazily. if coalesce path touches freed pages there might be a double-free window under concurrency. putting a quick sanitizer build is probably fastest to confirm. I can queue a debug build on canary-02.

Marisol Cardenas: perfect — @Jon please upload heapshots to share, @Tanya debug build would be great. I'll collect dmesg + oom_kill logs and tag in the thread. Thanks :pray:
